\abstract{\textbf{Motivation:} Exact pairwise alignment returns an optimal alignment under the chosen costs, so its results never depend on a heuristic's cut-offs, and it is the reference against which heuristic aligners are judged. Yet no exact algorithm is fastest on every workload: diagonal transition wins on near-identical pairs, bit-parallel band doubling on long divergent reads, and inter-sequence vectorisation on batches of short pairs.\\
\textbf{Results:} We present dinara-align, an exact aligner that chooses the algorithm for each pair as it runs, without giving up optimality. Three rules make these choices safe. A switch suggested by a runtime estimate is taken only once the current search has spent a small fixed share of the least work the alternative could need, so estimates inflated by errors clustered at read ends cannot abandon searches that would have finished. A gap-affine alignment starts a second wavefront search only when measured work shows that two searches would be cheaper than one, a rule we prove preserves optimality. Short pairs in batches are aligned in narrow bands whose optimality each vector lane certifies. On one Intel Skylake-X core and 25 datasets, from 250~bp reads to 1~Mbp pairs, dinara-align was the fastest exact aligner at unit costs, up to 2.4 times faster than A*PA2 on ultra-long nanopore reads and 2.5 and 5.7 times faster than WFA on Illumina and HiFi reads, and at gap-affine costs the fastest on every dataset any tool completed, 1.3 times faster than WFA on Illumina reads.\\
\textbf{Availability and implementation:} dinara-align is free software under the Mozilla Public License 2.0, available at \url{https://github.com/kokyriakidis/dinara-align} with C, C++, Python and command-line interfaces.}
